classification.difficultyReason: Find an equilateral triangle's altitude using Pythagoras, then sum the areas of two triangular and three rectangular faces.

content.prompt: The base of a right prism of height $12\text{ cm}$ is an equilateral triangle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the side length of the triangle is $6\text{ cm}$, use Pythagoras’ theorem to calculate the height of the triangle.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the base into two lengths of $3\text{ cm}$. Let the triangle's height be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2+3^2&=6^2\\h^2&=36-9\\h^2&=27\\h&=3\sqrt3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the surface area of the prism.

answer.short:
$(216+18\sqrt3)\text{ cm}^2$

Add the areas of the two triangular ends and the three rectangular faces.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of each triangle}&=\frac12\times6\times3\sqrt3\\\text{Area of each triangle}&=9\sqrt3\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of each rectangle}&=6\times12\\\text{Area of each rectangle}&=72\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}S&=2\times9\sqrt3+3\times72\\S&=(216+18\sqrt3)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
